body_html:
How to think about it

Living things are made mostly of water, which is a solvent and transport medium. Carbohydrates (sugars, starch, cellulose) give energy; lipids (fats and oils) store energy and form membranes; proteins build cells and act as enzymes; nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) carry genetic information.

Enzymes are biological catalysts. Each enzyme works best at an optimum temperature and pH; high temperatures denature the enzyme, changing the shape of its active site. Food tests: iodine for starch (blue-black), Benedict's for reducing sugars (orange-red) and Biuret for protein (purple).

Example

Which test shows starch?

Iodine solution

Answer: the colour changes from yellow-brown to blue-black

Example

Why does an enzyme stop working at 70 °C?

Look at its shape.

Answer: it is denatured

Common mistakes

  • Thinking enzymes are used up in a reaction.
  • Thinking all fats are unhealthy.
  • Mixing up the Benedict's and Biuret tests.

faq.q: Why do we need iron in our diet?
faq.a: To make haemoglobin, which carries oxygen in red blood cells; too little iron causes anaemia.
